items.plain: Don't run each other down, because judging a fellow believer sets you above God's law. There is only one lawgiver, who can save or destroy, so who are you to judge anyone?
items.core_idea: Only God may judge; we have no right to

items.plain: You plan next year's business as if sure of it, yet you don't know what tomorrow brings, for your life is a passing mist. Say instead, "If the Lord wills, we will live and do this."
items.core_idea: Life is brief; make plans subject to God's will

items.plain: Be patient until the Lord comes. A farmer waits patiently for the rains and the harvest; be patient like that too, and steady your hearts, because the Lord's coming is near.
items.core_idea: Wait patiently, like a farmer, for the Lord

items.plain: If you are suffering, pray. If you are happy, sing praise.
items.core_idea: Pray in suffering; sing praise in joy

items.plain: Admit your wrongs to each other and pray for each other so you can be healed. A good person's earnest prayer has great power.
items.core_idea: Confession and prayer for one another bring healing

items.plain: God tells Jeremiah he knew and chose him before birth. Jeremiah protests that he is too young to speak; God says not to plead youth, to go and speak, and not to fear, for God is with him.
items.core_idea: God chose you before birth and goes with you

items.plain: God says his people have done two wrongs: they left him, the source of living water, and dug their own cracked tanks that cannot hold water.
items.core_idea: Leaving God for empty substitutes that hold nothing

items.plain: I am in agony, my heart pounding and trembling inside me. I cannot stay quiet, because I have heard the trumpet and the alarm of war.
items.core_idea: Anguish of heart at the sound of war

items.plain: God says: stop at the crossroads and look; ask for the old, proven paths and which is the good way. Walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.
items.core_idea: Seek the old good way and find rest

items.plain: If only I could find comfort in my sorrow! My heart is weak inside me.
items.core_idea: Longing for comfort in deep sorrow

items.plain: I am wounded by my people's wound and mourn: is there no healing balm, no doctor, so why aren't they healed? I wish my eyes were a spring of tears to weep day and night for the dead.
items.core_idea: Grieving for others' suffering, longing for healing

items.plain: God says the wise, the strong and the rich should not boast of what they have. If anyone boasts, let it be in knowing God, who acts with kindness, justice and right, which he delights in.
items.core_idea: Boast only in knowing God, not wisdom, strength, wealth

items.plain: My wound is grave, but I said, "This is my grief, and I must carry it." My home is torn down, my children are gone, and there is no one left to help me rebuild.
items.core_idea: Accepting a grief that must be carried

items.plain: Lord, I know people cannot steer their own lives. Correct me, God, but gently, not in anger, or you will crush me to nothing.
items.core_idea: We cannot direct our steps; correct me gently

items.plain: God, you are just, yet let me ask why the wicked prosper and traitors live at ease. You planted them and they flourish; they speak of you, but their hearts are far from you.
items.core_idea: Why do the wicked prosper?

items.plain: If racing men on foot has worn you out, how will you race horses? If you only feel safe in peaceful country, how will you cope in the wild Jordan thickets?
items.core_idea: If small trials tire you, harder ones await

items.plain: I wish I had never been born, Mother: everyone fights with me. I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
items.core_idea: Cursed by all though I have wronged no one

items.plain: Your words were my joy, and because of you I sat alone, apart from the merrymakers. Why does my pain never end, and will you fail me like a stream that runs dry?
items.core_idea: Joy in God's word, yet lonely unending pain

items.plain: God says those who trust in people and turn from him are like a desert shrub that never sees good. Those who trust God are like a tree by a river: unafraid of heat, green, fruitful even in drought.
items.core_idea: Trust God and flourish like a well-watered tree

items.plain: The human heart is more deceptive than anything, and deeply sick. Who can understand it?
items.core_idea: The human heart deceives and cannot be fathomed

items.plain: Someone who gets rich unjustly is like a partridge sitting on eggs it did not lay. The riches will leave him halfway through life, and at the end he will be shown a fool.
items.core_idea: Wealth gained wrongly is lost; the gainer proves a fool

items.plain: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, because you are the one I praise.
items.core_idea: Only God's healing truly heals

items.plain: At the potter's house I watched a pot go wrong in his hands, so he reshaped it into another, as he saw fit. God then says Israel is like that clay in his hands.
items.core_idea: God can reshape us as a potter reshapes clay
items.extended_text:
Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making something on the wheels. When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it. Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
“House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says Yahweh. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.

items.plain: Lord, you persuaded me and overpowered me, and now everyone mocks me for your message. Yet if I try to stop speaking, it burns like fire in my bones and I cannot hold it in.
items.core_idea: God's word burns within and cannot be held in

items.plain: Why was I ever born, only to see trouble and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?
items.core_idea: Why was I born to sorrow and shame?

items.plain: God asks the king: does building with fine cedar make you a king? Your father ate and drank, yet did what was just and fair, and defended the poor and needy; that is what knowing God means.
items.core_idea: Knowing God means doing justice for the poor

items.plain: God says his plans for you are for peace, not harm, to give you hope and a future. Call and pray and he will listen; seek him with all your heart and you will find him.
items.core_idea: God plans hope for you; seek him and find

items.plain: God appeared to me long ago and said, "I have loved you with a love that lasts forever, so I have drawn you to me with kindness."
items.core_idea: God loves you with an everlasting love

items.plain: God says a cry is heard: Rachel weeping for her children, refusing comfort, because they are gone. Then God tells her to stop weeping; her work will be rewarded, there is hope, and her children will come home.
items.core_idea: Weeping mother told her children will return

items.plain: God says: I have given the weary soul its fill, and refreshed everyone who is sorrowful.
items.core_idea: God refreshes the weary and the sorrowful

items.plain: God says: I am the Lord, the God of every living being. Is anything too hard for me?
items.core_idea: Nothing is too hard for God

items.plain: God says: call to me and I will answer, and show you great, hidden things you do not know.
items.core_idea: Call to God and he will answer

items.plain: God repeats Baruch's complaint that God has added sorrow to his pain, and that he is worn out with groaning and finds no rest.
items.core_idea: Worn out by sorrow and finding no rest

items.plain: God says: leave your orphaned children with me; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
items.core_idea: God will care for orphans and widows

items.plain: My people have been like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and sent them wandering over the hills, until they forgot where their place of rest was.
items.core_idea: Misled people lost and far from their rest

items.plain: Don't lose heart or be afraid of the news you hear. One year brings one report, the next year another, with violence and rulers fighting each other.
items.core_idea: Don't lose heart at alarming news

items.plain: Job says he was born with nothing and will die with nothing. The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away, and may the Lord's name be blessed.
items.core_idea: God gives and takes away; bless him still

items.plain: When Job's three friends heard of his disaster, they came to comfort him. Seeing him unrecognisable, they wept, tore their robes and sat on the ground with him seven days and nights, silent, because his grief was so great.
items.core_idea: Friends sat silently with Job in his grief

items.plain: Job asks why people in misery are kept alive, longing for a death that does not come. His groans pour out like water; what he feared has happened, and he has no ease, no quiet, no rest.
items.core_idea: Why is life given to those in misery?

items.plain: Job's friend says: you have taught many and strengthened weak, stumbling people with your words. But now trouble has come to you, and you lose heart and are shaken.
items.core_idea: The comforter falters when trouble reaches him

items.plain: Resentment kills the fool, and jealousy kills the naive.
items.core_idea: Resentment and jealousy destroy the foolish

items.plain: Trouble doesn't sprout from the soil like a weed; people are born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
items.core_idea: Trouble is part of being human

items.plain: Job asks what strength or future he has to make waiting worthwhile, since he is not made of stone or bronze. He has no help left in him, and good sense has been driven away.
items.core_idea: Too exhausted to wait any longer

items.plain: Someone who is about to collapse should be shown kindness by his friend, even if he has stopped fearing God.
items.core_idea: A friend owes kindness to one who is collapsing

items.plain: Job says human life is forced labour, like a hired worker's. He has been given months of misery and weary nights; lying down, he longs for morning and tosses and turns until dawn.
items.core_idea: Months of misery and sleepless nights

items.plain: Job says his days fly faster than a weaver's shuttle and pass without hope. He asks God to remember that his life is only a breath; he will never see good again.
items.core_idea: Life is a breath passing without hope

items.plain: Ask the generations before us and learn what their ancestors discovered, for we are newcomers who know nothing and our days are a shadow. Won't they teach you from their hearts?
items.core_idea: Learn from the wisdom of past generations

items.plain: Job says his days race by without good. If he tries to forget his complaint and cheer up, he still dreads his sorrows; he knows God won't clear him, so why struggle in vain?
items.core_idea: Trying to cheer up while dreading one's sorrows

items.plain: Job says: I am sick of my life. I will let my complaint pour out and speak from the bitterness of my soul.
items.core_idea: Weary of life, speaking out of bitterness

items.plain: Job's friend promises he will lift his face without shame and stand firm without fear. He will forget his misery like water that has flowed past; darkness will become morning, and hope will make him secure.
items.core_idea: Misery will pass like water; hope brings safety

items.plain: Those who are comfortable look down on people who suffer misfortune; they think disaster is meant for those already slipping.
items.core_idea: The comfortable scorn those who suffer

items.plain: Ask the animals and they will teach you; ask the birds and they will tell you. Speak to the earth and it will teach you, and the fish of the sea will explain.
items.core_idea: Creation itself teaches, if you ask

items.plain: If only you would keep completely quiet! That would be wisdom.
items.core_idea: Silence would be wiser than your words

items.plain: A human being lives only a few days, full of trouble. He blooms like a flower and is cut down; he slips away like a shadow and does not last.
items.core_idea: Human life is short and full of trouble

items.plain: There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again. Even if its root grows old and its stump dies, at the scent of water it will bud and put out new shoots.
items.core_idea: A cut-down tree can sprout again

items.plain: Job calls his friends miserable comforters full of empty words; in their place he would strengthen them, not lecture. Yet whether he speaks or keeps silent, his grief does not ease.
items.core_idea: Miserable comforters; grief that will not ease

items.plain: Even so, the righteous keep to their path, and those with clean hands grow stronger and stronger.
items.core_idea: The righteous hold on and grow stronger

items.plain: My days are over, my plans broken off, and so are the hopes of my heart.
items.core_idea: My days are over and my plans broken

items.plain: My relatives have gone, and my close friends have forgotten me.
items.core_idea: Abandoned by family and friends

items.plain: Job says his closest friends loathe him and those he loved have turned against him. Wasted to skin and bone, he begs them to have pity on him, for God's hand has struck him.
items.core_idea: Abandoned by friends, begging for pity

items.plain: Job says: I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end he will stand upon the earth.
items.core_idea: My Redeemer lives and will stand at last

items.plain: Why do wicked people live long and grow powerful? Their children thrive around them, their homes are safe from fear, and God does not punish them.
items.core_idea: Why do the wicked live safe and prosper?

items.plain: One person dies strong, comfortable and well fed; another dies bitter, never having enjoyed good. Both lie down alike in the dust, covered by worms.
items.core_idea: Death levels the fortunate and the bitter alike

items.plain: Job says he looks east, west, north and south and cannot find God anywhere. But God knows the path he takes, and when God has tested him, he will come out like gold.
items.core_idea: God knows my way; testing will refine me

items.plain: As long as I live I will not give up my integrity. I will hold on to doing right and never let it go; my conscience will not accuse me.
items.core_idea: Holding on to integrity until death

items.plain: Where can wisdom be found? It is not in the deep or the sea, it cannot be bought with gold, silver or jewels, and it is worth more than rubies.
items.core_idea: Wisdom is priceless and cannot be bought

items.plain: God told humankind: reverence for the Lord is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.
items.core_idea: Revering God is wisdom; shunning evil, understanding

items.plain: Job longs for the old days when God watched over him and lit his way through darkness, when God's friendship filled his home, his children were around him, life overflowed, and he was honoured in the city.
items.core_idea: Longing for past days of God's closeness

items.plain: I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame. I was a father to the poor, and I looked into the case of strangers.
items.core_idea: I served the blind, the lame, the poor

items.plain: Job wept for people in trouble and grieved for the poor, yet when he hoped for good, evil came, and when he waited for light, darkness came. His heart is restless, and days of suffering have arrived.
items.core_idea: I hoped for light, and darkness came

items.plain: Job says he made a promise with his own eyes, so how could he look lustfully at a young woman?
items.core_idea: A covenant with my eyes against lust

items.plain: A young man says he held back from speaking to his elders, thinking age should teach wisdom. But understanding comes from God's breath in a person; greatness and age don't make someone wise or just.
items.core_idea: Wisdom comes from God's spirit, not age

items.plain: Has anyone ever said to God that they are guilty and won't do wrong again, and asked to be taught what they cannot see?
items.core_idea: Admit guilt, ask to see, and stop doing wrong

items.plain: No one asks, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night and makes us wiser than the animals and birds?"
items.core_idea: God gives songs in the night, yet none seek him

items.plain: Don't let wealth lure you into anger or a big bribe lead you astray. Would your riches or all your strength keep you safe when trouble comes?
items.core_idea: Wealth and strength won't save you in distress

items.plain: Stop, and think about the wonderful works of God.
items.core_idea: Pause and consider God's wondrous works

items.plain: God asks Job where he was when the earth's foundations were laid, and tells him to answer if he understands. Who set its measurements and its cornerstone, while the morning stars sang and the angels shouted for joy?
items.core_idea: Where were you when God made the earth?

items.plain: Job answers God that he is insignificant and has nothing to say, and puts his hand over his mouth. He has spoken once, even twice, and will say no more.
items.core_idea: Humbled before God, I fall silent

items.plain: God says: even now, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning. Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to God, who is gracious, merciful, slow to anger and full of love.
items.core_idea: Return to God with a torn heart

items.plain: God says: I will repay you for the years the locusts ate, the swarms I sent among you.
items.core_idea: God will restore the years that were lost

items.plain: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
items.core_idea: Darkness cannot overcome the light

items.plain: The wind blows where it wants; you hear it but don't know where it comes from or goes. That is how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
items.core_idea: Those born of the Spirit are like the wind

items.plain: God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. God sent him not to condemn the world but to save it.
items.core_idea: God gave his Son to save the world

items.plain: Everyone who does evil hates the light and avoids it, so their deeds won't be exposed. But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light, so it is clear their deeds were done in God.
items.core_idea: Evil hides from light; truth comes into it

items.plain: Jesus tells her that whoever drinks this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst; it becomes in them a spring welling up to eternal life.
items.core_idea: Jesus offers water that ends all thirst

items.plain: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
items.core_idea: Worship God in spirit and truth

items.plain: The saying is true: one person sows and another reaps. I sent you to harvest what you did not work for; others did the labour, and you have benefited from it.
items.core_idea: We reap what others have sown

items.plain: Jesus asked a man ill for thirty-eight years if he wanted to be well; the man said no one would help him into the pool. Jesus told him to take his mat and walk, and he was healed at once.
items.core_idea: Do you want to be made well?
items.extended_text: A certain man was there, who had been sick for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.” Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.” Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked.

items.plain: How can you believe, when you seek praise from one another and not the honour that comes from the only God?
items.core_idea: Seeking human praise blocks faith in God

items.plain: Jesus says: whoever comes to me I will never turn away.
items.core_idea: Jesus turns no one away

items.plain: Don't judge by appearances; judge fairly.
items.core_idea: Judge rightly, not by appearances

items.plain: Leaders brought Jesus a woman caught in adultery, and he told them whoever was without sin should throw the first stone, so they all left. He told her he did not condemn her, and to go and sin no more.
items.core_idea: Let the sinless throw the first stone

items.plain: You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
items.core_idea: The truth will set you free

items.plain: Seeing a man blind from birth, the disciples asked whose sin caused it, his or his parents'. Jesus said neither sinned; it happened so that God's works could be shown in him.
items.core_idea: Suffering is not always punishment for sin

items.plain: Jesus says: I am the good shepherd, who gives his life for the sheep. A hired hand who doesn't own them runs when the wolf comes and leaves them scattered, because he doesn't care for them.
items.core_idea: The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep

items.plain: Jesus tells her he is the resurrection and the life: whoever believes in him will live even after dying, and whoever lives and believes in him will never die. He asks if she believes this.
items.core_idea: Jesus is the resurrection and the life

items.plain: Mary fell at Jesus's feet weeping: if he had been there, her brother would not have died. Seeing her and the others weeping, Jesus was deeply moved and troubled, asked where they had laid him, and wept.
items.core_idea: Jesus wept with those who grieved

items.plain: Jesus says: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays a single seed. But if it dies, it produces a great harvest.
items.core_idea: A seed must die to bear much fruit

items.plain: Jesus says his soul is troubled, and asks whether he should pray to be saved from this hour. But this hour is the very reason he came.
items.core_idea: Troubled, yet facing the hour he came for

items.plain: Jesus says that since he, their Lord and teacher, washed their feet, they should wash each other's feet, following his example. A servant is not above his master, and they are blessed if they act on this.
items.core_idea: Serve one another as Jesus served

items.plain: Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another as he has loved you. Everyone will know you are his disciples by your love for each other.
items.core_idea: Love one another as Jesus loved you

items.plain: Jesus says not to let your hearts be troubled, but to trust in God and in him. His Father's house has many rooms; he goes to prepare a place for you and will come back for you.
items.core_idea: Don't be troubled; a place is prepared for you

items.plain: Jesus says: I leave you peace, my own peace, not the kind the world gives. Don't let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
items.core_idea: Jesus gives a peace unlike the world's

items.plain: Jesus commands: love one another as I have loved you. There is no greater love than to give your life for your friends.
items.core_idea: No greater love than dying for friends

items.plain: Jesus says you will weep and grieve while the world rejoices, but your sorrow will turn to joy, like a mother who forgets her labour pains once her child is born. No one will take that joy away.
items.core_idea: Your sorrow will be turned into joy

items.plain: Jesus says they will scatter and leave him, yet he is not alone, because the Father is with him. In the world you will have trouble, but take heart: he has overcome the world.
items.core_idea: Take heart: Jesus has overcome the world

items.plain: From the cross, Jesus saw his mother beside the disciple he loved and told each of them to treat the other as mother and son. From then on, that disciple took her into his home.
items.core_idea: From the cross, Jesus gives his mother a son

items.plain: Jesus tells Thomas: you believe because you have seen me. Blessed are those who believe without having seen.
items.core_idea: Blessed are those who believe without seeing

items.plain: Jesus tells Peter: when you were young you dressed yourself and went where you liked. When you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you don't want to go.
items.core_idea: In old age others will lead you

items.plain: Jonah prays that the waters closed over him and he sank to the roots of the mountains, shut in forever, yet God brought his life up from the pit. When he was fainting, he remembered the Lord.
items.core_idea: From the depths, God brought my life up

items.plain: God asked Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry?"
items.core_idea: Is your anger justified?

items.plain: God says: be strong and brave, as I have commanded you, and don't be afraid or discouraged. The Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
items.core_idea: Be strong and brave; God goes with you

items.plain: Not one of the good things God had promised Israel failed; every one came true.
items.core_idea: Every good promise God made came true

items.plain: Joshua says he is about to die. They know in their hearts that not one of the good things God promised them has failed; every one has come true.
items.core_idea: Not one of God's good promises has failed

items.plain: If you don't want to serve the Lord, choose today whom you will serve, your ancestors' gods or the gods of this land. But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.
items.core_idea: Choose today whom you will serve

items.plain: But you, dear friends, keep building yourselves up in your holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit. Keep yourselves in God's love as you wait for the mercy of Jesus Christ that brings eternal life.
items.core_idea: Build up your faith and stay in God's love

items.plain: Deborah sings to herself: march on, my soul, and be strong.
items.core_idea: March on, my soul, with strength

items.plain: The trees wanted a king, but the olive, fig and vine each refused to give up their good gifts to rule. Only the bramble accepted, offering shade but threatening fire if refused.
items.core_idea: The worthy decline power; the worthless seize it

items.plain: Delilah asks Samson how he can say he loves her when his heart is not with her.
items.core_idea: Love means the heart is truly with you

items.plain: Judith prays to God: you help the oppressed, support the weak, protect the abandoned, and save those who have no hope.
items.core_idea: God helps the oppressed and the hopeless

items.plain: The once-crowded city sits alone like a widow, a princess turned slave, weeping all night with no one to comfort her. Her friends have betrayed her and become her enemies.
items.core_idea: Desolate, betrayed and with no one to comfort

items.plain: Does it mean nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like mine, which the Lord brought on me in his fierce anger.
items.core_idea: Is there any sorrow like my sorrow?

items.plain: Look, Lord, I am in distress, and my heart churns within me because I rebelled badly. Outside the sword kills, and at home there is only death.
items.core_idea: In distress, heart churning over my wrongs

items.plain: Get up and cry out in the night, pouring out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to him for the lives of your children, fainting from hunger in every street.
items.core_idea: Pour out your heart before the Lord

items.plain: I had lost all peace, strength and hope, but I call this to mind and so I have hope. God's love keeps us from ruin; his mercies are new every morning, and great is his faithfulness.
items.core_idea: His mercies are new every morning

items.plain: The Lord is good to those who wait for him and seek him. It is good to hope and wait quietly for the Lord to save.
items.core_idea: Wait quietly in hope for the Lord

items.plain: The Lord will not reject anyone forever. Though he brings grief, he will show compassion out of his great love, for he does not willingly cause suffering or grief.
items.core_idea: God does not reject forever; compassion follows grief

items.plain: Let us examine our ways and return to the Lord. Let us lift our hearts and our hands to God in heaven.
items.core_idea: Examine our ways and return to God

items.plain: Waters closed over my head and I thought I was finished, so I called your name, Lord, from the deepest pit. You heard me, came near, and said, "Don't be afraid."
items.core_idea: From the depths I called, and God said: don't fear

items.plain: Our hearts have lost their joy, and our dancing has turned to mourning. The crown has fallen from our head; how terrible for us, for we have sinned.
items.core_idea: Our dancing has turned to mourning

items.plain: You, Lord, reign forever, so why have you forgotten us for so long? Bring us back to you and we will return; make our days new as they were before.
items.core_idea: Bring us back, Lord, and renew our days

items.plain: Mary praises the Lord and rejoices in God her Saviour, who has noticed his humble servant. Every generation will call her blessed, for the Mighty One has done great things for her, and his name is holy.
items.core_idea: My soul praises God, who lifted the humble

items.plain: The crowds asked John what they should do. He answered: whoever has two coats should give one to someone with none, and whoever has food should do the same.
items.core_idea: If you have two, share with one who has none

items.plain: Soldiers asked John what they should do. He told them not to extort money by force or make false accusations, and to be content with their pay.
items.core_idea: Take nothing by force; be content with your pay

items.plain: Jesus answered that it is written: people don't live on bread alone, but on every word of God.
items.core_idea: We do not live by bread alone

items.plain: Jesus reads: the Spirit of the Lord is on me, sending me to bring good news to the poor, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, give sight to the blind, release the oppressed, and announce the Lord's year of favour.
items.core_idea: Good news for the poor and broken-hearted

items.plain: Simon had fished all night and caught nothing, but when Jesus told him to let down his nets in deep water, he did it at his word. They caught so many fish that the nets began to break.
items.core_idea: After a fruitless night, trust brings a full net

items.plain: Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
items.core_idea: Those who weep now will laugh

items.plain: Jesus says to those listening: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
items.core_idea: Love your enemies and bless those who curse you

items.plain: Treat others exactly as you would want them to treat you. Loving only those who love you earns no credit, because even sinners do that.
items.core_idea: Treat others as you want to be treated

items.plain: Don't judge, and you won't be judged; don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Set others free, and you will be set free.
items.core_idea: Don't judge or condemn; set free and be freed

items.plain: Why notice the speck in your brother's eye and ignore the plank in your own, offering to fix his while blind to yours? You hypocrite: first remove your own plank, then you will see clearly to help him.
items.core_idea: Fix your own faults before judging others

items.plain: A good person brings good out of the good stored in their heart, and an evil person brings evil out of the evil stored there. What fills the heart comes out of the mouth.
items.core_idea: The mouth speaks what fills the heart

items.plain: Whoever hears Jesus's words and acts on them is like a man who built his house on rock, which the flood could not shake. Whoever hears but doesn't act built without foundation, and his house fell in ruins.
items.core_idea: Build your life on hearing and doing

items.plain: No one who puts a hand to the plough and keeps looking back is fit for God's Kingdom.
items.core_idea: Don't look back once you've committed

items.plain: A man was robbed and left half dead, and a priest and a Levite saw him and passed by on the other side. But a Samaritan felt compassion, bandaged his wounds and took him to an inn.
items.core_idea: The Samaritan who stopped and showed compassion

items.plain: Martha, busy serving, complained that her sister Mary sat listening at Jesus's feet instead of helping. Jesus said Martha was anxious about many things when only one is needed, and Mary had chosen the good part.
items.core_idea: Anxious about many things when one is needed

items.plain: Jesus teaches them to pray: Father in heaven, may your name be holy, your Kingdom come, your will be done. Give us our daily bread, forgive our sins as we forgive others, and keep us from temptation and from evil.
items.core_idea: The Lord's Prayer: how Jesus taught us to pray

items.plain: Keep asking and you will receive, keep seeking and you will find, keep knocking and the door will open. Everyone who asks, seeks and knocks will receive, find and be let in.
items.core_idea: Ask, seek, knock, and it will be given

items.plain: God forgets not even one cheap sparrow, and every hair on your head is counted. So don't be afraid: you are worth more than many sparrows.
items.core_idea: God counts every hair; don't be afraid

items.plain: Jesus warns: watch out and guard against greed, because a person's life is not made up of how much they own.
items.core_idea: Life is not measured by possessions

items.plain: Life is more than food and clothes; God feeds the ravens, who neither sow nor store, and you are worth far more. Worry can't add an inch to your height, so why worry about the rest?
items.core_idea: Worry adds nothing; God feeds the ravens

items.plain: Sell what you own, give to the poor, and store up treasure in heaven that no thief or moth can reach. Where your treasure is, your heart will be too.
items.core_idea: Where your treasure is, your heart is

items.plain: Much will be required of whoever has been given much, and even more will be asked of whoever has been trusted with much.
items.core_idea: Much given means much required

items.plain: A man wanted to cut down a fig tree that had borne no fruit for three years. His gardener asked for one more year to tend and fertilise it, and to cut it down only if it still bore nothing.
items.core_idea: One more year of care before giving up

items.plain: At a wedding feast, take the lowest seat rather than the best, so your host may move you up with honour instead of down in shame. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
items.core_idea: Take the lowest seat; the humble will be raised

items.plain: Who builds a tower without first sitting down to count the cost? Otherwise, having laid the foundation and been unable to finish, people will mock: this man began building but couldn't finish.
items.core_idea: Count the cost before you begin

items.plain: Anyone who lost one sheep of a hundred would leave the ninety-nine, search until it was found, and carry it home rejoicing. Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine who need no repentance.
items.core_idea: Heaven rejoices over one lost one found

items.plain: Whoever is faithful in small things is faithful in big things too. Whoever is dishonest in small things is dishonest in big things too.
items.core_idea: Faithful in little, faithful in much

items.plain: No servant can serve two masters; he will hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
items.core_idea: You cannot serve God and money
